m1-hole-ratio.title: Family 1: hole ratio ceiling, as a run-time ratio, with a mutation proof and a one-line action
m1-hole-ratio.imperative: Commit holes/entities as a generous ceiling ratio (a canary for a catastrophic docstring-extraction regression, not a documentation-completeness gate -- ordinary content edits must never trip it). Measure the real ratio on this repo AND on f1Brainz (read-only, different scale) to confirm the ceiling holds at both. Add a pytest test (name containing 'baseline') asserting the ratio on a fresh build of this repo. Prove the check can fail: mutate a copy of render.py so docstring extraction breaks (e.g. summary_of always returns None) and show the ratio blows past the ceiling (red), then restore and show the real corpus passes (green). State in the test/module docstring what a human does when this fires (open render.py's docs/doc_body wiring first). Attest c1 with the mutation-proof evidence, then advance c2 (the new test passes standalone).

postconditions.statement: mutation proof: ceiling trips on a broken-extraction mutant (red), holds on the real corpus (green) -- manual attest with evidence
postconditions.satisfied_by: Mutation-proof: HoleRatioBaselineFalsifierTests.test_baseline_ceiling_holds_on_an_intact_map (positive control, ratio 0.0) and test_baseline_ceiling_trips_when_docstring_extraction_breaks (render.summary_of mutated to always return None via mutated_package -- ratio goes to 1.0, crosses the 0.90 ceiling, assertGreater passes). Real corpus (HoleRatioBaselineTests): fresh scratch build of this repo, holes 2525 / entities 3753 = 0.673, under 0.90. f1Brainz (read-only, manual check): holes 8603 / entities 15037 = 0.572, under 0.90. python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k baseline -q --color=no -> 4 passed.

postconditions.statement: new baseline hole-ratio test passes standalone

constraints: ratio only, never an absolute count
state the action line in code

m2-ascii-provenance.title: Family 2: template-ASCII by exact-line provenance (never substring matching)
m2-ascii-provenance.imperative: Statically scan render.py's own AST for every literal string segment the module authors itself (Constant string nodes, and the literal segments of f-strings -- excluding interpolated {expr} parts, which carry source content and must NOT be censored). Assert every such literal is ASCII. This is exact-line provenance by construction: a literal render.py writes itself is template text; anything reaching a page through an f-string substitution is source content and is out of scope. Add a pytest test (name containing 'ascii'). Prove it can fail: a mutated copy of render.py with one non-ASCII character spliced into a literal (e.g. an em-dash in REFS_LEGEND) must be caught; the real render.py must pass. State the one-line action (open render.py, find the literal, replace the character) next to the check. Attest c1 with the mutation-proof, advance c2.

postconditions.statement: mutation proof: a spliced non-ASCII literal in a mutated render.py copy is caught; the real render.py passes -- manual attest with evidence
postconditions.satisfied_by: Mutation-proof: TemplateAsciiProvenanceFalsifierTests.test_ascii_scan_catches_a_non_ascii_character_spliced_into_a_template_literal (em-dash spliced into REFS_LEGEND's own literal text -- caught) and test_ascii_scan_stays_blind_to_non_ascii_text_reaching_a_page_through_interpolation (non-ASCII EXTERNAL value threaded through an f-string {expr} part -- zero offenders, proving the scan is exact-provenance not substring matching). Real render.py: TemplateAsciiProvenanceTests passes, zero offenders among 322 non-docstring literal string Constants. python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k ascii -q --color=no -> 3 passed.

constraints: exact-line/token provenance derived from render.py's own AST, never a hand-maintained list, never a substring match against rendered pages
the 386 existing non-ASCII pages (source-reproduced prose) must NOT be touched or newly flagged

m3-recall-floor.title: Family 3: edge recall per predicate (calls/reads/writes), hand-labeled sample, floor stated with its derivation
m3-recall-floor.imperative: Build a small, hand-authored fixture module exercising real-shaped calls, reads and writes (module-level constant reads, cross-module calls, self.attr writes, subscript writes) with every edge enumerated by hand as ground truth (no SCIP oracle available -- stdlib only, and SCIP is blind to writes anyway per DESIGN_SPEC TS7, so every predicate including writes is derived the SAME way: this hand count). Run the real extractor over the fixture and compute recall = matched/total per predicate. Commit a floor per predicate as a pytest test (name containing 'recall'), stating the derivation (small hand-labeled fixture, N edges per predicate) and its confidence plainly in the test docstring. Prove it can fail: a mutated extractor copy that drops one predicate's emission (e.g. writes) must push that predicate's recall below its floor; the real extractor must pass. Attest c1, advance c2.

postconditions.statement: mutation proof: a predicate-dropping extractor mutant fails its floor; the real extractor passes all three floors -- manual attest with evidence
postconditions.satisfied_by: Mutation-proof: RecallFloorFalsifierTests.test_recall_floor_trips_when_the_extractor_drops_a_predicate (extract._store's self._ref(t,"writes") anchor mutated to "reads" -- writes recall drops to 1/3=0.333, under the 1.0 floor; calls/reads recall unaffected, proving the falsifier is scoped). Real extractor: RecallFloorTests passes, 4/4 calls, 4/4 reads, 3/3 writes = 1.0 recall on the 11-edge hand-labeled fixture (RECALL_GROUND_TRUTH, verified by hand-trace against extract.py's own resolution rules R1-R8). python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k recall -q --color=no -> 3 passed.

constraints: a floor for EVERY predicate including writes
state plainly that the floor is derived from a small hand sample, never an unstated one
do not lean on an oracle that is blind to writes to justify the writes floor

m4-churn-ratio.title: Family 4: churn ratio (map diff lines / source diff lines), 3x ceiling, measured on a local edit AND the never-before-measured widely-referenced-symbol rename
m4-churn-ratio.imperative: Measure churn = map-tree diff lines / source diff lines on TWO real edits against this actual repo, via an isolated git worktree (never the main worktree): (a) an ordinary local edit to a low-fan-in function, (b) an actual rename of the real corpus's highest-fan-in internal symbol (identify it by inbound edge count from a fresh build; do not guess). Report BOTH measured ratios honestly. Treat the 3x ceiling as a hypothesis under test, not a foregone conclusion -- do NOT widen it to force the rename to pass, and do NOT drop the rename measurement if it is inconvenient. Add pytest test(s) (name containing 'churn'): assert the ceiling for whichever edit(s) the real measurement actually supports; if the rename measurement exceeds 3x, encode that as a stated, honest finding (not a silently-passing or silently-dropped assertion) and say so plainly in the RESULT. Attest c1 with both measured ratios, advance c2.

postconditions.statement: both ratios measured and reported (local edit, widely-referenced rename); 3x ceiling confirmed or falsified per case, stated honestly -- manual attest with evidence
postconditions.satisfied_by: Both ratios measured honestly on the real corpus via isolated git worktrees (never the main worktree), commit bd932921. LOCAL EDIT: discovery.is_mappable docstring edit -- 14 map diff lines / 11 source diff lines = 1.27x, under 3x. RENAME (never measured before this gate): highest-fan-in internal symbol identified by inbound scan (not guessed) -- tests.test_checklist_engine:gated, 212 distinct caller entities all within that one file, renamed to gated_plan -- 466 map diff lines / 458 source diff lines = 1.02x, under 3x. Ceiling CONFIRMED on both, not falsified; not widened, not dropped. Structural reason stated in thresholds.py: a pure rename changes ~1 line per call site on both source and map sides, so the ratio stays near 1x regardless of caller count even though PAGE count touched (217/3865) looks large in isolation. ChurnRatioTests/ChurnRatioFalsifierTests (fast synthetic fixture, same unit) added to tests/test_code_map.py as the CI-committed mechanism test; the expensive real-corpus worktree measurement is evidence in this RESULT, following g5's measure_split.py precedent, not a re-run-every-time test. python -m pytest tests/test_code_map.py -k churn -q --color=no -> 3 passed.

constraints: ratio of diff LINES, matching the cycle-4 trial's own unit (map diff lines / source diff lines), never an absolute page or line count
never widen the ceiling to force a measured finding to pass
never drop the rename case because it is inconvenient
isolated git worktree only, never edit the main worktree's tracked files

Attest c1, advance c2.

postconditions.statement: closing selector collects the new tests by name; full suite green; fresh build+check 7/7 exit 0 -- manual attest with evidence
